title: Process the Compression Tree Level by Level
real_world_story: A data-compression system needs to inspect its encoding tree level by level to analyze how encoded symbols are distributed across different depths.

real_world_connection.input_represents: A binary encoding tree stored in level-order
real_world_connection.target_represents: The nodes visited from the top level to the deepest level
real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Using a queue to visit every node level by level

problem_statement: Given a binary tree represented in level-order where -1 represents a missing node, print all existing node values using Breadth First Search traversal.
task: Traverse the binary tree level by level from the root and print the values of all existing nodes.
input_format: The first line contains an integer N, the number of positions in the level-order representation. The second line contains N space-separated integers. A value of -1 represents a missing node.
output_format: Print the existing node values in Breadth First Search order separated by spaces. If the tree is empty, print -1.
constraints: The first position represents the root

examples.explanation: The nodes are visited level by level: 1, then 2 and 3, then 4, 5, and 7.
Breadth First Search visits each existing node from the highest level to the lowest level.

expected_algorithm.name: Tree BFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Breadth First Search uses a queue to process tree nodes level by level, making it suitable for analyzing the structure of an encoding tree by depth.

hint: Start with the root node in a queue.
Remove the front node from the queue and process it.
Add its existing children to the queue.
Continue until the queue becomes empty.
real_world_takeaway: Tree BFS allows compression systems to inspect hierarchical encoding structures level by level and understand how data is distributed across tree depths.
